html:
The Itazipco, called Sans Arc by French traders, are one of the seven divisions of the Lakota, part of the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ or Sioux. The name means without bows.

Like other Lakota they were mounted bison hunters on the northern plains in the 1700s and 1800s, often camping near their close allies, the Miniconjou. They fought in the wars of the 1870s, including the Battle of the Little Bighorn in 1876.

After the wars they settled on what became the Cheyenne River Indian Reservation in South Dakota, where they still live with the Miniconjou, the Hunkpapa and others.
